title: Saxophone ideas, stock arrangements and recording in New York
summary: Reed players took tone from popular 1920s sax bands, and stock arrangements were trimmed; Barbarin cannot recall one New York recording.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Why did guys like Nicholas and Darnell Howard, when they'd play those sax choruses, when would they get their ideas?

Well, they used to listen to a, what's this guy named, played sax. He was very popular. Around the 20s, in the 20s, early 20s. Who did he play with? Rudy, we'd off. Rudy, we'd off. Rudy, we'd off. And, uh, Ross Garman, band. I mean, those guys, listen to those bands, you know. And they used to, and you try to get tone like those guys, you know. You know, and, uh, we played a lot of stocks and they would, you know, scratch out a lot of them. A lot of stuff in arrangement on the stocks, you know. They had a small arrangement and maybe played a last eight or something like that for the intro. And going to the chorus and then we'd go into another part, maybe they had three parts maybe. And we'd just use two parts, you know. Like that. Have an arrangement, make it different.
Where were these records made? You remember? I don't know.
